evals.prompt: Show me all my IP addresses
evals.expected_output: Lists all IPs grouped by type with tunnel, location, and connection status
expectations: Calls list_addresses with the user's auth token
Groups addresses by type (static_public, static_private, static_ipv6)
Shows address, location, tunnel name, connection status, and persistence
Presents output in a readable table format

evals.prompt: Get me a dedicated public IP on the London server
evals.expected_output: Leases a dedicated public IPv4 on the London server
expectations: Checks live entitlements (access/status) or list_ip_reservations for a free dedicated IP slot
Calls servers endpoint to find the London server hostname
Calls lease_public_ipv4 with the correct server and profile params
Explains that the dedicated IP persists across reconnections
Shows the newly assigned IP from ip_address and says a reconnect is needed when requires_reconnect is true
If refused with feature_required (dedicated_ip) or a full-slots 409, explains the add-on and shows upgrade_url instead of retrying

evals.expected_output: Rotates the user's public IP to a new address
expectations: Calls list_addresses to find the current public IP
Notes that a public IPv4 cannot be rotated (rotate_address takes static_private or static_ipv6 only) and offers the supported option
Warns user that the old IP will be released for good and a new one assigned, and that anything pointing at it must be updated
Asks for confirmation before rotating
Calls rotate_address only for a static_private or static_ipv6 address the user confirms, never for a static_public one

evals.prompt: Create a profile called Gaming and apply it to my desktop tunnel
evals.expected_output: Creates a Gaming profile and applies it to the desktop tunnel
expectations: Calls servers to list available servers for the user to choose
Calls create_saved_profile with profile_name=Gaming and the chosen server
Calls list_tunnels to find the desktop tunnel's tunnel_token
Warns that load_profile replaces all of the tunnel's settings with the profile's snapshot
Calls load_profile with the tunnel_token and new profile_id
If create_saved_profile returns feature_required (saved_profiles), explains Saved Connections is a Pro feature

evals.prompt: Show my saved profiles and delete the unused one
evals.expected_output: Lists profiles and deletes the unused profile after confirmation
expectations: Calls list_saved_profiles to list all profiles
Identifies profiles where in_use is false, and notes that a disconnected tunnel may still be bound to one
Does not print in_use_tunnel_token values
Asks user to confirm which profile to delete
Calls delete_saved_profile with the correct profile_id
Relays reconnect_message if the response has needs_reconnect

evals.prompt: Move my static private address 10.4.2.9 onto my Office profile
evals.expected_output: Assigns the address to the profile and reports any reconnect or site mismatch
expectations: Calls list_addresses and list_saved_profiles to find the address and the Office profile_id
Calls assign_address with address=10.4.2.9, type=static_private and profile_id of Office
If the response is a 409 site_mismatch, explains that the address and profile are at different locations and offers update_location=1 instead of retrying blindly
If needs_reconnect is true, shows reconnect_message and names reconnect_device

evals.prompt: Save my laptop tunnel's current settings as a profile called Travel
evals.expected_output: Snapshots the tunnel into a new profile and reports whether the tunnel is now bound to it
expectations: Calls list_tunnels to find the laptop tunnel_token
Calls save_profile with tunnel_token and profile_name=Travel
Reports the new profile_id and explains the bound flag (whether the laptop tunnel now uses the profile)
If refused with feature_required (saved_profiles), explains Saved Connections is a Pro feature and shows upgrade_url

evals.prompt: Apply the Tinfoil Hat mode to my desktop tunnel
evals.expected_output: Warns about the REPLACE effects and gets confirmation before apply_mode
expectations: Calls list_tunnels (and list_addresses) to show the desktop tunnel's current settings and addresses
Warns that apply_mode resets every setting it does not name and detaches the saved profile
Warns that a dedicated public IPv4 (a paid add-on address) bound through the profile is released
Asks for explicit confirmation before calling apply_mode
Handles feature_required (modes or a Pro setting) by showing upgrade_url instead of retrying

evals.prompt: Update my Travel profile with the current settings of my laptop tunnel
evals.expected_output: Saves a new profile with save_profile instead of re-snapshotting; never sends re_snapshot
expectations: Does not send re_snapshot=1 to update_saved_profile (it deletes the profile)
Offers save_profile from the laptop tunnel to a new profile, and asks before deleting the old Travel profile
Calls only endpoints in the manifest

evals.prompt: Take the dedicated IP off my Gaming profile, I don't need it there any more
evals.expected_output: Explains the difference between unlinking and giving the address up, then acts
expectations: Explains that release_ip_reservation only unlinks the IPv4 from the profile: it stays on the account and still uses a dedicated IP slot
Explains that release_address with type=static_public gives the address up for good, and that this cannot be undone
Asks which of the two the user wants and confirms before calling it
Calls release_ip_reservation with ip_address, or release_address with address and type=static_public, as the user chose

evals.prompt: Load my Office profile onto my laptop tunnel
evals.expected_output: Tries load_profile after confirmation; on 409 profile_in_use shows the message, names the tunnel that holds the profile, and offers the two safe ways out
expectations: Warns that load_profile replaces all of the laptop tunnel's settings and asks for confirmation before calling it
On a 409 profile_in_use, shows the message and names the tunnel that holds the profile (resolved from in_use_tunnel_token through list_tunnels inside the shell) and its device (in_use_by)
Does not print in_use_tunnel_token or any other tunnel_token
Does not follow release_action and does not disconnect or release anything on its own
Tells the user to disconnect the named tunnel and retry, or to pick another profile
